channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Zimbabwe’s processing for white gold deepens with another sulphate plant
item.description: Construction for another lithium sulphate plant in Zimbabwe has begun, as demand for lithium globally continues to surge.

item.title: 10 African countries with the highest diesel prices in February 2026
item.description: When diesel prices rise, it affects more than just vehicles at the pump; markets, farms, and homes throughout the continent.

item.title: Nestlé starts layoffs in South Africa as 16,000 global jobs are cut
item.description: Nestlé SA has started issuing retrenchment notices to over 400 employees in South Africa as part of a global reorganisation focused on four core divisions, according to sources familiar with the matter.

item.title: Top 10 African countries with the lowest diesel prices in February 2026
item.description: In Africa, diesel is more than simply a commodity; it is the engine of many of the continent’s economies.

item.title: After close to three years, U.S. lifts sanctions on Mali officials amid improving AES ties
item.description: The United States has lifted sanctions imposed in July 2023 on three senior Malian officials over their links to Russia’s Wagner mercenary group, in a move that signals a diplomatic reset with the military-led governments of the Sahel.

item.title: Zak Calisto moves into insurance as regulator backs King Price deal
item.description: A South African tech billionaire is expanding into the insurance sector after the country’s competition watchdog recommended approval of a transaction that will give him an interest in King Price.

item.title: Top 10 African countries with the strongest currencies in February 2026
item.description: In global finance, a robust currency serves as a significant indicator, transcending a mere exchange rate figure, particularly within select African countries.

item.title: Sudan moves to reshape Africa’s gold market with 2,000-tonne reserve target
item.description: Sudan is poised to make a major mark on Africa’s gold sector, with new estimates suggesting its reserves could exceed 2,000 tonnes, far above the official figure of 1,500 tonnes.

item.title: Dangote signs $1B deal with Chinese firm to expand projects across seven African countries
item.description: Dangote Cement Plc (DCP), a subsidiary of Dangote Industries Limited, has signed a $1 billion agreement with China’s Sinoma International Engineering to construct new plants and expand existing facilities across Africa.

item.title: China overtakes South Africa as world’s top chrome processor amid soaring power costs
item.description: South Africa has lost its long-held position as the world’s leading processor of chrome into ferrochrome to China, as surging electricity prices continue to batter the country’s energy-intensive smelting sector.
